pr_title: Fix handling of symlinked device descriptors in keyboard_remote and move remaining sync io to executor thread pool
pr_body: Fixes #28982 (regression introduced by https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/27761 where symlinked paths were not handled properly by the new asynchronous device detection)
pr_comments: In principle the full path of the device could change on disconnect/reconnect, so any stored paths would need to be updated in any case.
All of the remaining sync io should be moved to executor jobs now (this was only present during setup and device connect/disconnect at least)

issue_context.title: Keyboard Remote broken
issue_context.body:
**Home Assistant release with the issue:**
0.102.1

**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**
0.101.3

**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**
Hass.io @ Raspberry Pi 4

**Integration:**
https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/keyboard_remote/

**Description of problem:**
The Keyboard Remote integration does not work for me after updating to 0.102. Remote and keyboard automations are not triggered, no `keyboard_remote_command_received` events in Developer Tools. Tried with two keyboards that worked before, and if I revert to 0.101.3 they work again as expected.

**Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml` entries and (fill out even if it seems unimportant):**
```yaml
keyboard_remote:
- device_descriptor: '/dev/input/by-id/usb-flirc.tv_flirc-event-kbd'
  type: 'key_up'
```

**Traceback (if applicable):**
```

```

**Additional information:**
comments: Hey there @bendavid, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`keyboard_remote`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L169) for? Thanks!

There could be an issue with "by-id" paths and the new asynchronous device detection.  I'll take a look and try and fix it.  In the meantime you may try using the device path rather as "/dev/input/event[n]"
Tried with `/dev/input/event0` and it works on 0.102.1!

my Keyboard remote connects fine initially.  However, when it comes back from hibernate mode, it connects to RPI4B fine (since I could see from bluetoothctl that it is connected) but somehow HA does not recognize it. Automation related to keyboard remote do not get triggered.  After HA is restarted (not the RPI4B), the keyboard remote works perfectly fine

Is there a way to debug this?  I have provided more details in the community thread

[keyboard remote does not automatically reconnect](https://community.home-assistant.io/t/keyboard-remote-does-not-automatically-reconnect/151717)
Are you sure it's working as expected outside of home assistant?  ie if you don't grab the device with home assistant, can it send keys to the console after a disconnect/reconnect cycle?

Yes, it does send the keys to the console.  I try the cat /dev/input/event0  and it registers the keystrokes from the numeric key.  Also, after every connect/disconnect the "Bluetoothctl" prompt dutifully registers the change.  
However, it is not the same for the automation within the HA.  As I explained in the community post - whenever, the numeric pad disconnects, there is no "keyboard_remote_disconnected"  or "keyboard_remote_connected" event captured.  These are only captured during the shutdown or restart of the Home Assistant. 
Observation:  After the numeric pad disconnects and I restart the Home Assistant, the keyboard is connected again.  My assumption is that it picks up the latest event files as registered in /proc/devices.  **Is there anyway to refresh the HA's Keyboard Remote to poll the /proc/devices from the latest /proc/devices?**   Or rather **how does the Keyboard Remote keep and instance of event files?**
Any update or any other info required to help solve my problem? I just cannot understand why it cannot reconnect when either Device Name or the Device Descriptor is given

The detection of disconnect/reconnect is based on inotify, so it looks at the file object in /dev/input/event0.

Does this device disappear and reappear as expected when the device is disconnected and reconnected?

Yes, the device does disappear and reappear as expected as I could see in the linux console. Also there is a small led in keyboard which turns red and green as expected. I found out that the actual input files I think get changed everytime a reconnect is made. The below is the output of cat /proc/bus/input/devices
The input# in the below S:......./input/input0  always gets a new number.  Is this the source of the problem?

```
I: Bus=0005 Vendor=xxxx Product=1234 Version=011b
N: Name="Namando Keypad Keyboard"
P: Phys=xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx
S: Sysfs=/devices/platform/soc/fe201000.serial/tty/ttyAMA0/hci0/hci0:11/xxxx:xxxx:xxxx.xxxx/input/input0
U: Uniq=xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx
H: Handlers=sysrq kbd leds event0
B: PROP=0
B: EV=120013
B: MSC=10
B: LED=1f
```

Just here to tell that I have the same problem and to confirm the issue. If more information is needed I could step in. I'm also using the `by-id` path. I use hassio and checked from within the container, as I was expecting the container to be the issue. I could verify, that the general device path was available from within the container though. Using not `by-id` path circumvents the issue currently.

I have investigated further, I got another similar remote. And this  remote somehow reconnects properly and promptly to HA. I am able to get consitent notification even after prolonged sleep.  So I guess, it is to do with the device rather than the HA or RPI.  The device I used is similar to this:
[Car Bluetooth Audio Adapter](
https://www.amazon.com/Onewell-Bluetooth-Adapter-Steering-Compatible/dp/B07ZYRWZGY/ref=sr_1_6?keywords=car+bluetooth+audio+remote&qid=1577090510&sr=8-6)

Bit it is clearly a regression. If I downgrade to version 100 I don't have this issue. However on version 103 I have it. I think you are not referring to the 'by-id' device path issue but rather a connection issue, where the device works initially and then stops. I think these are two different problems here.
